docs.title: Streaming and buffering
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: While Terragrunt logs stdout from OpenTofu/Terraform in real time, it buffers each line of stdout before logging it. This is because Terragrunt needs to be able to buffer stdout to prevent different units from interleaving their log messages.

docs.title: Problem
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: The recommended best practice for Terragrunt usage was previously that users defined two types of terragrunt.hcl files for any significantly large code base:

docs.title: Recommended Solution
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: To simplify Terragrunt usage and make it more clear what the root configuration is, it is now recommended that users rename the root terragrunt.hcl file to something else (e.g. root.hcl).

docs.title: Additional Considerations
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: If you use Scaffold and Catalog, you may need to use additional flags to control how new units are generated. It was previously a safe assumption that most users would leverage a root terragrunt.hcl file, and thus, the default behavior was to generate a new unit that would look…

docs.title: Strict Control
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: To enforce this recommended pattern, you can also enable the root-terragrunt-hcl strict control to throw an error when Terragrunt detects that a root terragrunt.hcl file is being used.

docs.title: Future Behavior
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: For now, warnings will be emitted when this pattern is detected in order to encourage users to change to the new pattern, but this behavior will be an explicit error in a future version of Terragrunt.

docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: The following sections outline the steps you may need to take in order to migrate from Terragrunt \<= v0.18.x to Terragrunt 0.19.x and newer:

docs.title: Move from terraform.tfvars to terragrunt.hcl
docs.heading_path: Migration guide > Move from terraform.tfvars to terragrunt.hcl

docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh

docs.snippet: When we were using terraform.tfvars files for Terragrunt configuration, we were piggybacking on the fact that Terraform automatically loads variables from tfvars files to set variables for our modules:

docs.title: Use first-class expressions
docs.heading_path: Input variables to set for your Terraform module > Use first-class expressions
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Terraform 0.11 only allowed special behavior, such as function calls, using "interpolation syntax," where you wrapped the code with ${...}. Terragrunt included a handful of functions you could call using interpolation syntax, but _only_ within the terragrunt = { ... } block:

docs.heading_path: Using interpolation syntax outside of the terragrunt config did NOT work before
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh

docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh

docs.title: Background
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: As part of the redesign in #3445, several CLI adjustments have been made to improve user experience and consistency. This guide will help you understand the changes and how to adapt to them.

docs.title: Migration guide
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: All of the changes you need to make to adopt to this new CLI design involve changing how you invoke Terragrunt from the command line.

docs.title: Remove `terragrunt-` prefix from flags
docs.heading_path: Migration guide > Remove `terragrunt-` prefix from flags
docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: If you are currently using flags that are prefixed with terragrunt-, you will need to stop using that flag, and use a differently named one instead (usually the same exact flag with terragrunt- removed from the beginning, but not always).

docs.attribution: © gruntwork-io/terragrunt contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: If you are currently using environment variables to configure Terragrunt, you will need to stop using that environment variable, and use a differently named one instead (usually the same exact environment variable with TERRAGRUNT_ replaced with TG_, but not always).

docs.snippet: Previously, Terragrunt only supported orchestrating the tofu and terraform binaries as the main program being executed when Terragrunt was invoked.

docs.snippet: Previously, Terragrunt would automatically provision any backend resources defined in the remote_state block of a terragrunt.hcl file.

docs.snippet: Once Terragrunt supported the ability to define multiple includes, and to expose the values in includes as variables, users could optionally use named includes instead of a bare include.

docs.snippet: HCL parsing does not support the ability to parse HCL configuration and accept that a configuration block has zero or more attributes, so a workaround in Terragrunt internals was to parse the configuration, then rewrite it internally to avoid breaking backwards compatibility for…

docs.snippet: Especially on large projects, this extra work is not worth the performance penalty, and Terragrunt has deprecated support for bare includes.
